title: Alonso set for Dakar Rally return with Aston Martin
excerpt:
Fernando Alonso will compete in the Dakar Rally for Aston Martin in January 2027, marking his return to the event after seven years.

Alonso is set to drive the Aston Martin Dreadnought as part of a three-car challenge alongside nine-time World Rally Champion Sebastien Loeb and reigning World Rally Raid Champion Lucas Moraes.

The Spaniard will be joined by co-driver Marc Coma, a five-time Dakar motorcycle category winner who sat alongside Alonso during his 2020 debut in the event – in which he finished 13th overall.

With the 2027 Dakar taking place in the Sahara Desert between January 9 and 23 – beginning in Portugal and then racing through Morocco – Alonso will then turn his focus to the 2027 F1 season, with pre-season testing scheduled for February before the campaign gets underway in March.

"After deciding to continue racing in Formula 1 with the Aston Martin Aramco, I thought carefully about Dakar," said Alonso. "In the end, the decision became simple. I wanted to embrace the challenge completely and take on both Formula 1 and the Dakar Rally in the same year.

"In 2020, Dakar was one of the most challenging and enjoyable experiences of my career. I have enormous respect for this race and the specialists who have mastered it. Having Marc alongside me again is very important, and with Aston Martin, Prodrive, Sebastien and Lucas we have an exceptional team.

"Formula 1 remains my priority. But I am a racing driver, and challenges like this are why I love competing. I’m looking forward to seeing what we can achieve."

Alonso’s previous participation in the Dakar Rally occurred during his two-year hiatus from Formula 1 between 2019 and 2020, with the Spaniard also taking part in other feats such as the Indianapolis 500 as well as winning the World Endurance Championship.

title: Aston Martin showcase bespoke Las Vegas Grand Prix livery
excerpt:
Aston Martin have become the latest team to unveil a special livery for the Las Vegas Grand Prix, a collaboration with their Official Cloud Compute Partner CoreWeave.

Featuring shades of white and black alongside the team’s signature green, an announcement revealing the design states that the look was “inspired by the two organisation's shared ambition to Pioneer the Possible”, adding that it “celebrates CoreWeave's integration into the team, from the AMR Technology Campus to each race weekend”.

As well as adorning the AMR26, the design will also feature across the team’s garage and Lance Stroll's helmet during the event.

Jefferson Slack, Managing Director, Commercial and Marketing, Aston Martin Aramco, said: "The Las Vegas Grand Prix gives us a fantastic opportunity to showcase the strength of our collaboration with CoreWeave through this unique livery takeover. What makes this collaboration particularly exciting is the work happening behind the scenes.

"From helping our engineers make sense of race communications in near real time to identifying new directions in aerodynamic development, we're seeing how CoreWeave can change the way we operate.

"This is about more than technology for technology's sake. It's about giving our people the tools to challenge assumptions, discover new opportunities and keep pushing the boundaries of what's possible."

The livery reveals follows on from Williams’ unveiling of their own one-off design for Las Vegas.

title: Terry Crews on America's growing love for F1
excerpt:
Actor and former NFL player Terry Crews believes Formula 1's growing popularity in the United States is doing more than attracting new fans, with the sport encouraging Americans to embrace different countries and cultures.

Growing up in Flint, Michigan, Crews was surrounded by the automotive industry, with his father working for General Motors. That connection has since come full circle as the star of Brooklyn 99 has made regular appearances at races.

Formula 1's popularity in the United States has continued to grow ahead of the Las Vegas Grand Prix, the country's final race of 2026 season, its American fanbase has grown to 52 million, an 11% increase in 2025.

But Crews believes the sport's growing popularity is having an impact on Americans that extends beyond the racetrack.

"I wouldn't say [Formula 1] is becoming more American. In fact, what I would say is that Americans are becoming more Formula 1.

"The United States tends to be quite insular… When you look at the number one sport in the world, it's football, but if you talk to people in America, they say it's American football. They think the Super Bowl is the biggest sporting event in the world, and actually the World Cup is the biggest.

"Formula 1 has expanded America's minds. When you look at a lot of Americans, they don't even have a passport, because the United States is so big they feel like they're travelling. But because of Formula 1, there's now Americans saying, 'I'm going to Hungary, I'm going to Singapore, I'm going to Monaco.'

"There's so many Americans that I've run into that are like, 'Hey, I watched Drive to Survive, I knew Cadillac was in here. This is my first time out of the United States.'"

Crews is no stranger to international audiences himself, having enjoyed a career spanning television, film and professional sport. And it was F1's global appeal that initially drew him towards the championship.

"One thing that I love is being a worldwide person. It was very important to me, even in my entertainment career, that every project that I do reaches everywhere in the world, and I'll be honest, I'm actually bigger around the world than I am in the US.

"When I go to Brazil, Korea, the UK, or anywhere in the Middle East, it's gigantic, and that's one thing I love. It's a big world, and that's what turned me on about Formula 1 in the first place: the fact that it was a world sport."

Dressing for the occasion

Crews' appreciation for the different cultures on the F1 calendar also extends to his paddock wardrobe. The actor works alongside his friend and business partner, designer Nana Boateng, to create custom outfits for his appearances around the world.

And with races taking place in locations as different as Monaco, Austin and Las Vegas, Crews believes each occasion deserves its own look.

"Most of my [clothing] is custom, simply because my body does not fit off the rack. It took a long time to be able to do things like this, but I'm wearing one of the world's best menswear designers, my best friend and business partner.

"His name is Nana Boateng, and we go through the seasons and pick out what we're doing, how we look. Monaco can't look like Vegas, that can't look like Austin, especially when we're going to Formula 1 races.

"He's tailored my taste. Twenty years ago, I didn't dress like this. It's like hanging out with a wonderful chef. He elevates your taste. McDonald's won't work anymore."

And ahead of the Las Vegas Grand Prix, Crews is ready for even more Americans to take a bite and get the taste for F1.

title: Williams unveil special livery for Las Vegas Grand Prix
excerpt:
Williams have unveiled a special livery that will adorn their car for the Las Vegas Grand Prix weekend.

The one-off chrome look is a collaboration with the team’s title partner Atlassian, designed to shine under the lights as Alex Albon and Carlos Sainz take to the Las Vegas Strip Circuit. Both drivers will also sport custom race suits and gloves in line with the colour scheme.

In an announcement revealing the livery, Williams stated that the design is “the latest embodiment of Williams and Atlassian’s belief that the fastest way forward is knowing where you have been, which is central to the partnership”.

Team Principal James Vowles commented: “Our next step forward isn’t a matter of reinvention; it’s about evolving from where we’ve been, using the knowledge, context, and information our team shares.

“We’re proud to be working with Atlassian to unlock that near-50-year history and using it as fuel for our future. This spectacular livery reflects that and I’m looking forward to seeing it take to the track under the bright lights of the Vegas Strip.”

Mike Cannon-Brookes, Co-Founder and CEO, Atlassian, added: “The new Williams livery looks great in Las Vegas – but our partnership goes well beyond what you see on the track. We are helping Williams turn their ambition into execution.

“We’re working shoulder to shoulder with the team at Williams to build AI workflows on the Atlassian Teamwork Graph connecting their teams’ expertise, knowledge and projects so they can make smarter, faster decisions.”

title: 5 storylines we're excited about ahead of the Las Vegas GP
excerpt:
20 races down, three to go. The 2026 Formula 1 season is set to kick off the final triple-header of the year, and even with the winners of both championships already decided, there are plenty of storylines to get excited about.

Here are just a few of the talking points as the paddock heads to Las Vegas.

Lawson and Lindblad stay

Across the previous triple-header in Austin, Mexico City and Sao Paulo, there was a growing focus on the Racing Bulls driver line-up for 2027.

Arvid Lindblad’s impressive rookie season always looked likely to secure him a second year, as the teenager continues his development and looks to build on multiple point-scoring finishes. However, the other side of the garage appeared to have less certainty over what would happen next.

Liam Lawson has enjoyed an outstanding season, including a very solid three-race run at Red Bull in place of the injured Isack Hadjar at the end of August and early September. The New Zealander has also led the field outside the top four teams on numerous occasions and continued that form even when he didn’t have confirmation of a future seat.

With Racing Bulls weighing up whether to promote the talented Nikola Tsolov into a race seat in 2027, Lawson produced a run of four top seven finishes in five races, finishing ninth behind the two Mercedes, Ferrari, Red Bull and McLaren drivers in the middle of that stretch in Austin.

Alan Permane’s team confirmed the current pairing of Lawson and Lindblad will continue into 2027 last week, and now the focus will be on the progress Red Bull want to see from each moving forward.

Cadillac’s driver decision

It isn’t just at Racing Bulls where there has been uncertainty over a driver line-up, with Cadillac also considering their options.

Sergio Perez is already committed on a long-term contract, with an extension being announced in Mexico City as a reward for both his strong performances on track but also the work that Perez has been doing to try and push the team forward behind the scenes.

His team mate Valtteri Bottas was also signed for his experience to help develop Cadillac, but there were questions from the team regarding some of his performances during the year, and there was a clear replacement option being explored in the form of Colton Herta.

ANALYSIS: Why the F1 driver market might produce one last twist

The American former IndyCar star received a number of extra FP1 outings in order to help him secure the points required to apply for his FIA Super Licence, and duly reached that target last time out at Interlagos.

That gave Cadillac the ability to weigh up their options over whether they want to stick with Bottas - who is under contract - or give Herta his first opportunity to race in F1.

Ahead of another home race for Cadillac, a decision is understood to have been made, with the expectation that the team will continue with their current experienced pairing into 2027, and an announcement due during the Las Vegas Grand Prix week.

Camara gets another outing

There are so many driver stories to keep an eye on at the moment, and another is more immediate than the two above as Haas adapt to life after Esteban Ocon.

The Frenchman was replaced in the middle of the Mexico City Grand Prix race weekend by Ryo Hirakawa, and the experienced reserve driver duly earned himself a point on debut as he was able to take advantage of post-race penalties for others.

With Hirakawa racing in the World Endurance Championship at Monza the following weekend, Haas then took the opportunity to give their 2027 race driver Rafael Camara an early debut, with the Brazilian taking the seat for the Sao Paulo Grand Prix.

At the time, Haas made clear the decisions only related to those specific race weekends, and there had been no final call on who would drive for the remainder of the season. Theoretically, Haas could alternate between both Camara and Hirakawa, although they can’t turn to another option without requiring special dispensation from the FIA due to a rule limiting teams to four race drivers per season.

Haas have now confirmed Camara will retain the drive for the rest of the year as they get a head start on 2027, with the 21-year-old building on his first experience during a challenging Interlagos weekend.

Championship battles for drivers and teams

Mercedes wrapped up the Teams’ Championship at the last race in Brazil, one week on from Kimi Antonelli becoming the youngest Drivers’ Champion in history in Mexico. But that doesn’t mean there isn’t still plenty to play for.

From a teams’ perspective, so much of the focus is on who wins the title, but the prize money is paid out based on where each team finishes in the constructors’ standings, meaning each position below P1 still carries a huge amount of weight.

Our writers on Antonelli’s title success and what it means

Ferrari look well placed to wrap up second place overall, but behind that is a close battle for third between Red Bull and McLaren. The double podium at Interlagos allowed Red Bull to pull 17 points clear of McLaren, but it was Lando Norris who took victory in a sign of McLaren’s potential after introducing an upgrade in Brazil.

McLaren Team Principal Andrea Stella says there will be further additions in Las Vegas as they continue developing with 2027 in mind, and they could well help McLaren stay in touch with Red Bull entering the final rounds.

When it comes to the drivers’ standings, it’s more a case of pride being at stake, but Max Verstappen currently occupies second place behind Antonelli after a remarkable run of eight straight podiums - including three victories.

Verstappen is looking to extend his current tally of seven consecutive seasons finishing in the top three in the championship - an eighth would match Lewis Hamilton’s record - but there are just 33 points covering the Dutchman, George Russell, Hamilton, Charles Leclerc and Norris, with all five having won races this year.

A spectacular racing venue

We have seen all sorts of action in Las Vegas since the race joined the calendar in 2023, with last lap overtakes, wet qualifying sessions and reliability issues all playing a role in producing drama at different phases of the weekend.

The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a unique challenge for multiple reasons, not least the near-two-kilometre-long run along the Strip that sees the cars flashing past a number of the most iconic resorts in the city.

Racing under the lights means competitive track action taking place after dark as temperatures drop, and that means it is often the coldest race weekend of the year as well.

With teams having to juggle energy demands on a circuit with multiple long straights, it could well be another race weekend with plenty of overtaking right up until the final lap.

title: McLaren determined to take fight for P3 ‘down to the wire’
excerpt:
Racing Director Randy Singh is optimistic that McLaren can maximise their performance in the final three rounds and secure third place in the Teams’ Championship, but noted that they don’t “feel any less pressure than the last couple of season finales”.

After clinching back-to-back constructors’ titles in 2024 and 2025, McLaren slipped behind Mercedes and Ferrari in this season’s pecking order, and lost an additional spot to Red Bull during the recent triple header.

However, they received a crucial boost as Lando Norris made the most of their upgrades at Interlagos to take his third victory of the campaign, which could provide the momentum they need to overhaul Red Bull’s 17-point advantage in the standings.

Asked on the latest episode of F1 Nation whether they can close the gap, Singh replied: “We'll do our best to make sure it goes down to the wire and in our favour. We're treating it like a mini championship on our side, so we're just aiming to do our best at each race.

“I think it’s what saw us through both 2024/2025 Abu Dhabi races – there was a lot of pressure. We just try to focus on doing the best that we can in each area, and the result will take care of itself, hopefully.

“It's interesting because it doesn’t feel [like] any less pressure than the last couple of season finales to be honest. We've got three races as well, which is quite nice because we've got plenty of time to try and harvest as many points as we can.

“Everyone's excited and then we get straight into Las Vegas preparation as well. And this week everyone's pretty intense with seeing what we can learn from the last race – both in the dry and in the mixed conditions – and what we can do to prepare for Vegas. So, full activity and steam ahead.”

Since Las Vegas was added to the calendar in 2023, it’s become one of McLaren’s weaker tracks, with costly errors, a lack of pace and even a double disqualification limiting them to a total of just 17 points over three events.

They’re hoping to turn that form around when the paddock heads back to The Strip this week, especially as they have another chance to capitalise on the effective upgrades they introduced in Brazil.

“We all see it as a challenge and a big opportunity for us to really go and get a result at a circuit that we haven't had a good result at yet,” Singh explained. “And so we're all kind of approaching it with that kind of relish.

“We had some good upgrades on the car in Brazil, so we've got some work to do to still keep getting the most out of those. We're really approaching it from that underdog sense of, ‘we've not had a good one there, but we've got a good chance to have a really good result there [this year].

“The upgrades worked well – you can tell that also from Oscar [Piastri], who only had them from FP2 onwards because we missed FP1 in Brazil. Both drivers really quickly got up to speed again, especially Oscar. I think missing an FP1 session is tricky.

“We had the car in a good window in Brazil. We need to try and make sure we do the same in Vegas. It'll be much colder, I think, than it was in Brazil. The grip can be very low. Circuit characteristics are completely different as well.

“So we've got a lot of work to do to try and make sure that we hit the ground running, and that we keep optimising the package as it is now. It's not easy with these cars.

“Whilst we've had these cars now for the best part of a year, the upgrades, as Andrea [Stella] said before, are really quite significant. They changed the way the car behaves and we have to kind of re-learn some of that stuff each time.”

McLaren’s battle for P3 in the Constructors’ Championship was just one of the talking points that emerged in the Las Vegas Grand Prix preview, which saw Jolyon Palmer and James Hinchcliffe join F1 Nation host Tom Clarkson.

title: Haas confirm Camara to race for the team in Las Vegas
excerpt:
Haas have confirmed that Rafael Camara will again race for the team at the Las Vegas Grand Prix – following on from his Formula 1 debut last time out at his home event in Sao Paulo – while Ryo Hirakawa is also set to get behind the wheel during Free Practice 1.

Following Esteban Ocon’s departure during the Mexico City Grand Prix weekend, reserve driver Hirakawa stepped in for his maiden race at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez – ending the event with a point thanks to a P10 finish.

Camara – who was announced as one of Haas’ 2027 drivers in October – then made his own debut one week on at Interlagos, with the youngster managing to bring the car home amid challenging weather conditions.

Haas have since announced that the 21-year-old will again get behind the wheel of the VF-26 alongside Ollie Bearman in Las Vegas, offering another opportunity to gain further track time ahead of his maiden full-time campaign next season.

“I’m looking forward to getting back in the car in Las Vegas,” said Camara. “Brazil was a good learning experience, and now the focus is on building on that, improving step by step and making the most of every session.

“It’s a new circuit for me, so there’s a lot to learn, but I’ll do my best to keep progressing throughout the weekend.”

Hirakawa, meanwhile, will make his fourth FP1 appearance of the year for the squad in place of Bearman, two weeks on from the Japanese driver winning the 2026 World Endurance Championship with Toyota Racing.

Haas Team Principal Ayao Komatsu commented: “We're looking forward to kicking off the final triple header of the 2026 season at the famous Las Vegas strip. This street course offers very unique challenges, and we've got to be at our very best to perform there.

“In Brazil, our 2027 recruit Rafa Camara made his debut under extremely challenging conditions and showed us and the world why we signed him for 2027. We're looking forward to building on that for his second race weekend with us.

“Our reserve driver, Ryo Hirakawa, also put in an impressive performance when he was drafted in on Saturday morning in Mexico. He will be back in the car for FP1 in place of Ollie Bearman, now as the 2026 WEC World Champion.

“In recent races, we showed that we can perform at a very high level when everything is working well, and we're looking to get back to performing at the level we showed on Sunday in Mexico.”

title: Max Verstappen response to hilarious Red Bull radio: 'He doesn't speak English'
excerpt:
Max Verstappen might have won best radio message of 2026 in Brazil.

Max Verstappen had everyone laughing on Friday in Brazil with a team radio message about his engine. The Dutchman has since explained exactly what the problem was, joking his car "doesn't speak English".

The award for team radio of the 2026 season may already have been decided. On Friday at the São Paulo Grand Prix, the four-time world champion aired his frustrations over the clutch and engine braking on the RB22 by appearing to have a conversation with his own power unit.

Red Bull ultimately swapped the engine after the session, resulting in a grid penalty for Verstappen which saw him start in 21st before recovering to second.

Speaking to Viaplay, Verstappen looked back on the moment, explaining what exactly had gone wrong on board his car.

The Red Bull driver started off joking about the radio message before turning serious on the subject.

"I think he doesn't speak English," Verstappen laughed, when asked about talking to his engine.

"I'm still trying to figure out what language he does speak. I haven't tried Dutch yet; I don't know. He didn't respond very well..."

Max Verstappen reveals constantly changing problem

Verstappen then explained the technical issue behind the hilarious comments, with a driver very rarely if ever being heard on the radio speaking to their car.

"In some corners you downshift, it's fine, and you've got enough slip in the clutch," Verstappen began to explain. "But in the next corner you downshift and it's like the rear just locks up. That's the first problem."

"The other problem is when you go into a corner and come off the brake, the engine pushes through really hard. Then in the next corner it's like a handbrake again.

"I also told the team: you can change the whole car, but when that happens, it overrules everything. It's completely different in every corner, and that just makes it incredibly difficult."

title: Lewis Hamilton stripped of podium as Ferrari suffer intra-team collision - On This Day
excerpt:
The 2019 Brazilian Grand Prix was an absolutely crazy one! Penalties and intra-team clashes, it had it all.

Seven years ago today, Max Verstappen claimed one of the most dramatic wins of his career at Interlagos, as both Ferraris crashed out of the 2019 Brazilian Grand Prix and Lewis Hamilton was stripped of a podium finish by the stewards.

Verstappen converted pole position into victory, leading home Pierre Gasly and Carlos Sainz in a result few had predicted before the chequered flag.

Gasly, starting sixth for Toro Rosso, crossed the line 6.077 seconds behind the Red Bull driver to claim what remains the finest result of his career, while Sainz completed the podium for McLaren despite starting a lowly 20th on the grid, following a late engine change.

The result was shaped as much by misfortune for others as by the pace of the front-runners. Sebastian Vettel and Charles Leclerc, who had qualified second and fourth respectively, collided with six laps remaining while fighting over what was then third place.

Leclerc had gone around the outside of his team-mate into Turn 1, only for Vettel to find a tow down the Reta Oposta and drift into his path.

The contact broke Leclerc's right-front suspension and punctured Vettel's rear tyre, ending both cars' races on the spot.

The stewards investigated the clash after the race but opted not to take further action, ruling that both drivers had contributed to the incident and had each had a chance to avoid it.

Ferrari team principal Mattia Binotto summoned Vettel and Leclerc to Maranello in the aftermath, stating that responsibility for the crash was shared between the pair.

According to The Guardian, the team subsequently made clear that while its drivers remained free to race each other, prioritising the team's interests and avoiding on-track collisions was non-negotiable going forward.

Lewis Hamilton, who had started third, also saw his race unravel. On the penultimate lap, following a late restart, the Mercedes driver attempted a move around the outside of Alex Albon at Turn 10 for what was then second place.

The pair made contact, spinning Albon around and ending his afternoon. The stewards judged that Albon had been on the racing line and that Hamilton was predominantly to blame for attempting the move into a closing gap, handing him a five-second penalty and two penalty points on his licence.

The penalty dropped Hamilton from an on-track third to an eventual seventh in the final classification.

The Interlagos clash between the Ferrari drivers was later described as the culmination of mounting tension between Vettel and Leclerc that year over status within the team, a rivalry that would help shape Ferrari's direction for seasons to come, with Leclerc eventually handed a long-term extension and Vettel's Maranello career drawing to a close not long after.

title: Bernie Ecclestone criticises Ferrari's Italian 'politics' over latest title failure
excerpt:
Bernie Ecclestone has spoken out on his thoughts on Ferrari this season.

Bernie Ecclestone has claimed that Ferrari should have won this year's world championship, while suggesting team principal Fred Vasseur is overwhelmed by the job.

The former Formula 1 supremo made the comments to RTL/Sky Sports as Ferrari's 2026 campaign heads towards its conclusion still without a title.

Mercedes has run away with both championships this season, with Kimi Antonelli sitting top of the drivers' standings on 390 points after 20 rounds, well clear of Max Verstappen on 279.

Ferrari's Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton sit fifth and fourth respectively, with the Scuderia 142 points adrift of Mercedes in the constructors' table.

Ecclestone, who has long been a vocal critic of Ferrari's internal politics, argued the Maranello outfit possessed the fastest car on the grid this year but was let down by its own structure.

"Ferrari should have won the world championship this year," Ecclestone insisted. "They had the best car. So many different things went wrong.

"I've been saying for many years, ever since I convinced them to bring in a Frenchman as team principal: there are too many Italians.

"Everyone thinks they know better how to run the team, that it's being run incorrectly, and that they could do it better."

Fred Vasseur 'overwhelmed' by Ferrari leadership position

Ecclestone went further, turning his attention directly to Vasseur, who has led Ferrari since the start of the 2023 season.

"To be honest, he's a nice person, but simply overwhelmed by the task of running a team like Ferrari," added Ecclestone.

"Ferrari needs a very, very, very strong person who thinks about Ferrari from the moment they wake up until they go to sleep. [...] I wonder if he really devotes the majority of his thoughts to Ferrari."

The remarks arrive despite Vasseur and senior Ferrari management having previously pushed back on rumours of leadership instability, insisting that stability and working in calm conditions were what the team needed to succeed.

Vasseur himself has conceded that Ferrari knew from the season opener that its power unit was down on output compared to Mercedes and Red Bull, a deficit he said severely limited the team's title prospects despite a strong chassis.

Leclerc has echoed that technical explanation, pointing to a straight-line speed shortfall relative to Mercedes and Red Bull as the car's main handicap, while insisting Ferrari's wind tunnel correlation with on-track performance remained positive.

Whether that power unit deficit can be resolved for 2027, and whether Vasseur will be given further scope to restructure the team beneath him, remain open questions heading into the winter.

title: Ferrari replace Lewis Hamilton for Las Vegas GP first practice
excerpt:
Ferrari has confirmed that Dino Beganovic will replace Lewis Hamilton for first practice at the Las Vegas Grand Prix, fulfilling the final mandatory rookie session of Ferrari's 2026 campaign.

The Scuderia has now completed all four of its required rookie outings for the season.

Beganovic has already deputised for Hamilton in Spain and for Charles Leclerc in both Austria and Brazil, meaning this Las Vegas appearance closes out Ferrari's obligations under the expanded rookie rule.

Formula 1's sporting regulations, broadened from 2025, require every team to hand FP1 duties to a rookie, defined as a driver with no more than two grand prix starts, across at least two sessions per car each season.

That adds up to four mandatory FP1 appearances per team over the year.

The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is not typically viewed as a forgiving venue for rookie running. Unforgiving concrete walls, low initial grip and a track surface that evolves sharply from a green first practice to a heavily rubbered, cooler nocturnal session make set-up work unrepresentative, and teams have generally been reluctant to hand such a session to an inexperienced driver.

Ferrari, however, had little choice given the timing of its remaining commitment. Beganovic, a Ferrari Academy member since 2020, has built up FP1 mileage across the year and was recently confirmed to be stepping up into a full-time reserve and development role with the Scuderia from 2027.

He will not be the only reserve on duty in Las Vegas. Haas has also opted to field Ryo Hirakawa in FP1, standing in for Oliver Bearman as it too works through its rookie-running requirements before the season concludes.

title: McLaren striving to make 'peace' with Las Vegas after persistent struggles
excerpt:
McLaren boss Andrea Stella is optimistic heading into the Las Vegas Grand Prix, where he hopes the team can vanquish its Sin City demon.

Andrea Stella hopes McLaren can finally make "peace" with the Las Vegas Grand Prix this weekend, with recent upgrades offering encouragement ahead of a return to one of the team's most troublesome circuits.

The Woking-based squad has endured three difficult visits to Nevada, culminating in last year's double disqualification for excessive skid wear.

While Lando Norris' victory in São Paulo provided a timely boost, the long straights of the Las Vegas Strip Circuit will place different demands on the MCL40.

McLaren's shorter gear ratios have contributed to its limitations at circuits where outright top speed is particularly important. The lengthy flat-out section along the Strip therefore threatens to expose a weakness already evident at Monza and Baku.

Stella acknowledged that the layout presents a challenge as McLaren seeks to carry its improved form into the weekend.

"It's a very different circuit layout, Vegas, long straights," Stella told media, including RacingNews365.

"We have seen this in Monza; we have seen this in Baku: when the requirement is to develop top speed, McLaren is not necessarily the best car.

"We know that this also somehow relates to our gear ratios that are not ideal when you need to go above a certain level of top speed."

[Article continues below]

Upgrades offer McLaren hope

McLaren introduced a new front wing in Brazil to improve the car's predictability and driveability, with further parts due in Las Vegas.

Those developments also form part of its preparations for 2027, giving the team reasons for encouragement beyond Norris' Interlagos victory. Stella believes the lessons from Brazil can help McLaren extract more from its package in Nevada.

"But having said that, I think we approach Vegas with some optimism because the car is faster now," Stella added.

"I think this race will give us, and not only us, but everyone, I think, a bit of understanding of how to use the tyres, and where the car is good, where their car or our car is less good. So there's information to be capitalised on for Vegas as well."

[Article continues below]

Three years of frustration

Both McLarens exited Q1 in 2023, before Norris crashed after bottoming out. Oscar Piastri finished P10.

In 2024, tyre graining, understeer and a loss of aerodynamic efficiency when reducing rear-wing downforce contributed to Norris and Piastri finishing sixth and seventh.

Last year brought a stronger performance, with Norris taking pole before finishing second and Piastri fourth. However, both were disqualified after their rear skid blocks fell below the minimum permitted thickness. McLaren attributed the excessive wear to unexpected porpoising, which increased contact with the track.

"So, we look with some optimism, and also Vegas is... we want to go there and have a good result because it's probably been, of all the races on the calendar, the one that we've been struggling the most at," Stella said.

"And even last year, when we had a good race, we made our life bad with the problem that we had with the skid.

"So we look forward to Vegas, have a good result there, and finally be at peace with this venue."

title: Exclusive: Formula E chairman planning multi-company event extravaganza
excerpt:
Formula E chairman and co-founder Alejandro Agag is planning on a multi-company event extravaganza in 2028, holding the all-electric single-seater series and his electric powerboat series E1 on the same weekend at the same location.

Agag, who co-founded Formula E, founded two other all-electric categories. He founded the off-road Extreme E - now known as Extreme H - in 2021 and, most recently, E1 in 2024.

It had been planned for Monaco to host Formula E and E1 on the same weekend this year, although the Principality was against the idea of having two events on the same dates, preferring to stage them separately.

However, that only reignited talks of having Formula E and E1 take place on the same weekend at the same place, demonstrating the advancement of electric mobility on land and water.

Formula E and E1’s calendar both feature three of the same destinations: Monaco, Miami and Jeddah.

RacingNews365 understands Miami and Jeddah are the two most probable options for it to happen, with Monaco having declined hosting both on the same weekend this year.

The idea is for the events to take place on the same day at different times, allowing eyeballs to bounce from one to the other.

2028 joint event target

The problem with Miami, though, is both events taking place in very different locations. Formula E races at the Miami International Autodrome, while E1 is at Biscayne Bay 25 kilometres away.

From a different perspective, Jeddah is the most logical, with Formula E at the Jeddah Corniche Circuit and E1 at the Obhur North waterfront being just 13 kilometres from one another and both along the Red Sea.

"So we're really trying to make that happen," Agag exclusively told RacingNews365 in Miami at the E1 finale.

"We were actually trying to do it in Monaco this year, but Monaco prefers to have the event separately, I guess because maybe hotels and, like, this, they have two events. But it would be great to have both at the same time.

"So, potentially, Miami is one option. I mean, there are many options because we have places where we race that have the scenery. Tokyo, for example, could be incredible for having Formula E and E1 together.

"So, yeah, definitely, I think soon we will have a joint Formula E and E1 event."

The idea of both on the same weekend in the same city is currently being explored for as soon as 2028, with Agag hungry to turn the idea into a reality.

"We've been trying to do it next year," added Agag. "I think it's going to be 2028. We will coordinate the calendar with Formula E and try to make it happen in 2028."

title: Fernando Alonso teams up with motorsport legend as Dakar entry confirmed
excerpt:
Fernando Alonso has confirmed he will take part in the 2027 edition of the Dakar Rally.

The Spaniard will partner with two other champions for the entry, with his team-mates confirmed to be nine-time FIA World Rally champion Sebastien Loeb and reigning FIA World Rally Raid champion Lucas Moraes.

The trio will get behind the wheel of a competition-ready version of the Aston Martin Dreadnought, which was originally designed for the video game Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4.

It will mark Alonso's second entry in the Dakar Rally, having done so in 2020 while on a break from full-time competition in F1.

Over the last couple of months, Alonso insisted that he would not partake in the 2027 edition, insisting it was impossible to prepare for both F1 and Dakar at the same time.

However, his entry has now been confirmed, with Aston Martin fielding three cars at the event for the three champions.

Alonso will be supported at the event by co-driver Marc Coma, reigniting the partnership that occured at the Spaniard's last Dakar entry.

"After deciding to continue racing in Formula One with the Aston Martin Aramco, I thought carefully about Dakar," Alonso said.

"In the end, the decision became simple. I wanted to embrace the challenge completely and take on both Formula One and the Dakar Rally in the same year.

“In 2020, Dakar was one of the most challenging and enjoyable experiences of my career. I have enormous respect for this race and the specialists who have mastered it.

“Having Marc alongside me again is very important, and with Aston Martin, Prodrive, Sébastien and Lucas we have an exceptional team. Formula One remains my priority.

“But I am a racing driver, and challenges like this are why I love competing. I’m looking forward to seeing what we can achieve."

The 2027 Dakar Rally was originally scheduled to be held in Saudi Arabia, but due to the ongoing conflict in the region, a new route was designed.

It will now begin in Portugal and travel south and into Morocco, and cover almost 8,000 kilometres from January 9 to January 23.

Alonso's last entry in the Dakar Rally almost seven years ago saw him end the event in 13th place, with the overall winner being Carlos Sainz - the father of Alonso's F1 colleague Carlos Sainz Jr.

title: F1 drivers handed ‘brutal’ warning as crazy record at risk of breaking
excerpt:
Formula 1 drivers could be braced for the coldest race in the sport's history this weekend, with forecasts for the Las Vegas Grand Prix pointing to temperatures as low as four degrees Celsius.

The current record stands from the 1978 Canadian Grand Prix at Circuit Ile Notre-Dame, where ambient temperatures dropped to around five degrees.

Gilles Villeneuve won that race for Ferrari in near-freezing conditions, with podium finishers reportedly needing thick winter jackets on the rostrum afterwards.

Las Vegas has been no stranger to unusually cold conditions since joining the calendar in 2023, with track temperatures during past editions dropping as low as 12 to 15 degrees Celsius. This year's forecast appears to go several steps further.

Former F1 driver Jolyon Palmer addressed the reported four-degree forecast on the F1 Nation podcast.

"Every year when we come to Vegas, everyone's sort of scaremongering about how many layers we need to put on, whether the drivers need the sort of, like, overgloves to stop their hands freezing on the wheel," Palmer said.

"Four degrees would be, I think, a record for how cold a Formula 1 race has been. So, if it is, that's going to be pretty brutal. If it's not a record, it must be at least very close."

The Las Vegas tyre challenge

Palmer went on to explain why the cold poses such a specific challenge on the Las Vegas Street Circuit.

"And that's why the tyres just take a while to come in. The warm-up is pretty poor. It's a temporary circuit, obviously, and it's quite smooth asphalt. So, it really is a low-energy track for the tyres."

Pirelli has nominated its softest compound selection for the event, with the C3 as hard, C4 as medium and C5 as soft, in an attempt to help drivers generate heat.

But the Italian manufacturer has also warned that cold asphalt and limited surface grip promote front-end sliding, leaving degradation largely mechanical and raising the risk of graining, with the long full-throttle straights also stripping heat from the tyres before the braking zones that follow them.

Palmer expects the strategic picture to remain largely unchanged despite the extreme conditions.

"So, I see it being a one-stop pretty comfortably once again. And, yeah, the low-speed corners as well, they don't help to load up the tyres and put a load of energy through."

"So, slippy-slidey in Vegas, and when you've got the walls so close and you've got really high top speeds and big braking zones, there's loads of overtaking opportunities. There's loads of opportunities to make mistakes too, which is, I guess, the recipe for a good race if you're watching."

title: George Russell issues stern defence after crushing F1 title defeat
excerpt:
George Russell has denied he would change his approach if he could this year after suffering a title defeat to team-mate Kimi Antonelli.

Antonelli wrapped up his maiden championship at the Mexico City Grand Prix at the start of the month, a victory that came with little surprise due to the mammoth lead he had built up in the standings.

While Russell has suffered his share of reliability woes, the Mercedes driver has often struggled to match the performance of Antonelli.

The 28-year-old is now facing a battle to secure P2 in the standings, with Max Verstappen currently occupying the runner-up spot.

When asked if there was anything he would have done differently if he had the chance, Russell told media including RacingNews365: "I don't think so, no.

"You can't foresee the problems that you're going to face until you experience them.

"I did great preparation with the team, that helped me to win the first race of the season. When we have so little testing, so little practice in the cars, you're learning in the races.

"Then you learn what the problem is, and you need to give it one or two or three races to see the consistent trend.

"Then you've got time to try and understand 'how do I resolve this issue?' and then we have no practice to try all these new things.

"You've got to use the races to try all these new things and be comfortable with the changes."

[Article continues below]

Russell insists no regrets over 2026 approach

Russell has won three grands prix this year so far, while Antonelli has stood on the top step of the podium on nine occasions.

The Briton is now targeting a strong end to the campaign in order to build momentum for the 2027 season.

While his year unfolded in a disappointing way, Russell insists he has no regrets over his approach.

"I'm not pleased with how the season has gone, but I don't look back with any regrets," he said.

"I prepared as much as possible, more than anybody, I believe. I've bounced back from the tough moments.

"I worked as hard as possible to understand what the issues are and try and resolve them, and it's led us through this moment. That's sport, you can't win every year."

title: Ferrari warned over 'massive handicap' in F1 title hunt: 'The stuff of nightmares'
excerpt:
Ferrari has been warned that it faces a dilemma over managing its drivers if the team is in a position to win the F1 title next year.

In recent weeks, tension has been brewing between Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc, sprouting from a wheel-to-wheel battle on the opening lap of the Mexico City Grand Prix.

The Italian squad has endured a frustrating campaign and has once again not been involved in the fight for the championship, with Mercedes and Kimi Antonelli already sealing both titles on offer.

As it focuses its resources on 2027 in the hope of finally challenging for the crown, it was raised on the F1 Nation podcast that both drivers will be fighting for superiority and backing.

When asked if it is a strategy that Ferrari needs to adopt, former F1 driver Jolyon Palmer said: "It's what one of them needs, but I don't think you can say categorically it has to be Lewis for next year.

"They've been really even in terms of pace, points and just general performance. You can't say for next year it's going to be Lewis.

"I know we were talking about this earlier in the year, but that was when Lewis was sort of 30 points away from Kimi and Charles was like 50 points further back.

"But for next year, when everyone starts from zero, you can't go into that season thinking, 'We're going to use Charles as a number two driver'.

"They're going to have this fight, the start of next year is going to be exactly this, they're once again going to be out there to prove their superiority."

[Article continues below]

Both Hamilton and Leclerc talked through the matter ahead of the Sao Paulo Grand Prix to iron out any lingering concerns, insisting the matter is now behind them.

But Palmer insisted that tension will likely be reinstated in 2027 if either driver has a sniff at winning the championship.

"If they're having this level of tension, and they're not even fighting for a title, they're nowhere near it, imagine if they are fighting for a title," he said.

"For me, that is a massive handicap that Ferrari has going into next year.

"The driver lineup is like the stuff of dreams, but equally on the other hand, it could be the stuff of nightmares because controlling them is so tricky."

title: Toto Wolff adopts firm stance on prospect of Kimi Antonelli joining Ferrari
excerpt:
Toto Wolff insists he has zero per cent concern that Kimi Antonelli will one day leave Mercedes for Ferrari, pointing to the Italian’s loyalty and the team’s ability to deliver championship success.

Antonelli has become the first Italian to win the F1 drivers’ championship in 73 years, ending a wait stretching back to Alberto Ascari’s 1953 triumph with Ferrari.

His title also made him the youngest world champion in F1 history, with third place at the Mexico City Grand Prix securing the crown at 20 years and 68 days old. He is the first graduate of Mercedes’ junior programme to win the championship.

That success gives Italy a home-grown champion, although its newest title winner races for a rival of the country’s most celebrated team.

The prospect of an Italian world champion driving for Ferrari provides an obvious attraction, but Wolff sees no reason to fear Antonelli will be tempted away from Mercedes.

Asked by BILD how concerned he was that Antonelli might eventually want to race for Ferrari because of his nationality, the Mercedes team principal replied: "0.0 per cent."

Pressed on the reason for that confidence, he added: "Because Kimi and his family are loyal people."

Antonelli's championship has rewarded Mercedes' decision to entrust him with the seat vacated by Lewis Hamilton, whose own departure took him to Ferrari. The Italian has since delivered the title in only his second F1 season.

For Wolff, however, retaining Antonelli is about more than the strength of the relationship between the team and his family.

Challenged on whether loyalty was enough in F1's cutthroat environment, Wolff pointed to the competitive incentive for his driver to stay.

"In this case, I'm convinced, yes," he said. "But we don't rely solely on loyalty. This season has shown that we can win races and titles. That's the most important thing for every driver. Including Kimi. He belongs to Mercedes like wheels belong to a car.

"That's why, after winning his title, he said he couldn't imagine driving for any other team besides Mercedes."

[Article continues below]

Antonelli wins over Ferrari fans

Wolff also believes Antonelli's achievements are allowing him to build a following in Italy despite competing against Ferrari.

His victory at Monza provided a particularly significant example, giving the home crowd an Italian winner to celebrate even as Ferrari missed out.

Asked whether Antonelli could become more popular in Italy as a Mercedes driver than Michael Schumacher had been during his Ferrari years, Wolff answered: "Absolutely! He's Italian, after all."

When it was put to him that Antonelli does not drive for Ferrari, Wolff pointed to the reception his driver has received.

"Yes, but what Kimi has achieved through his natural manner and success is that Italy, while still passionate about its national team, Ferrari, has also opened its hearts and souls to this little Italian," he responded. "The Tifosi are now wearing Ferrari shirts with Mercedes caps.

"Monza was the perfect example. The spectators were actually disappointed that neither of the two red cars finished first, but they were thrilled that Kimi, one of their own, was standing on the top step of the podium."

title: Sergio Perez weighs in on Cadillac F1 driver decision ahead of 'crucial' period
excerpt:
Sergio Perez has stated there is not an "easy decision" for Cadillac to make over its driver line-up for the 2027 season.

Perez's position has already been confirmed, having recently signed an extension that will see him through at least the end of 2029.

While Valtteri Bottas was brought into the squad last year on a reported multi-year deal, Cadillac has been pushing for Colton Herta to acquire his super licence, which he successfully did last time out in Mexico City following his latest free practice outing.

Herta is looking to make the jump to F1 despite a disappointing Formula 2 campaign, and Perez insisted that his feedback as a development driver has been valuable.

"Well, I think he's doing a good job," Perez told media including RacingNews365.

"He's bringing good feedback to the team and good information, which is all we need from him.

"Obviously, doing FP1s is always very difficult to show your speed or the level you're at.

"But now I think he's having more time in the car and in the simulator, so we're starting to see more of his speed. Obviously, it's not my decision, but I think it will be down to Marcin to decide who they want in the car.

"I'm also working really well with Valtteri. I think he's been very unfortunate in a few races. There isn't an easy decision for the team."

[Article continues below]

Perez denies role in choosing 2027 team-mate

With Perez committed to the team for the long term, the Mexican is due to play a crucial role in the future of the new squad and aid its development as it seeks to climb the order.

However, the 36-year-old denied that he will assist in the choice of who occupies the second seat for 2027.

"No, not at all. I don't want to, either, because that's not my decision," he said.

"That's why we have someone like Marcin, who will be looking at all the data and information, and he will ultimately make that decision based on what he thinks is best for the future of the team.

"Obviously, we're in a period where we need to evolve extremely quickly. The next three or four months are really crucial in our preparation. So, yeah, I think it's down to him."

title: Liam Lawson handed crushing verdict over delayed Racing Bulls decision
excerpt:
Liam Lawson will continue with Racing Bulls for the 2027 F1 season, after the Faenza-based squad confirmed the New Zealander and Arvid Lindblad last week.

Lawson has been one of the stars of the campaign, whilst his team-mate has enjoyed a strong rookie year in the VCARB 03.

However, Racing Bulls left it late to announce both would stay put, with Red Bull junior and F2 drivers' title hopeful Nikola Tsolov also under consideration.

The Bulgarian will instead focus his efforts on reserve duties for the joint teams and carry out an extensive testing programme, likely in preparation for a full-time seat in 2028.

Although Lindblad was not confirmed either, it is widely accepted that Racing Bulls were weighing up whether to promote Tsolov now and drop Lawson.

That move would have proven unpopular given the 24-year-old's performances this year, which have the Red Bull sister team on the cusp of finishing fifth in the constructors' standings for the first time.

Lawson has scored 89 points and is best of the rest in the drivers' championship after those from the top four teams. That haul is more than Pierre Gasly and Franco Colapinto's combined 69 points, with their Alpine team sitting sixth in the table.

As such, Lawson was given emphatic backing after Racing Bulls finally confirmed his future, with 95 per cent of fans who voted in a recent poll by RacingNews365 voicing their support for the — albeit delayed — decision.

title: Williams unveil 'chrome' livery tweak for Las Vegas Grand Prix
excerpt:
Williams will run a bespoke one-off livery at the Las Vegas Grand Prix, developed alongside title partner Atlassian.

The chrome design features rainbow accents and navy detailing running across the bodywork and engine cover.

The reflective highlights have been placed specifically to catch the light under the floodlit Las Vegas Street Circuit, giving the cars a distinct look when they hit the track on Friday evening.

It's the latest special livery from Williams as it seeks to enjoy a successful weekend at an event it has a history at.

Williams won the inaugural Las Vegas Grand Prix back in 1981 with Alan Jones, and sealed Keke Rosberg's title there the following year.

“Our next step forward isn’t a matter of reinvention; it’s about evolving from where we’ve been, using the knowledge, context and information our team shares,” said team boss James Vowles.

“We’re proud to be working with Atlassian to unlock that near-50-year history and using it as fuel for our future.

“This spectacular livery reflects that and I’m looking forward to seeing it take to the track under the bright lights of the Vegas Strip.”
